planting.note: Plant with the crown set a couple of inches below soil level and keep the roots cool and shaded while the compact vine climbs a trellis, obelisk, or large container support into full sun.

directions: Minister is a compact large-flowered clematis bred from 'Hagley Hybrid' stock, producing abundant semi-double to double mauve-violet flowers suffused with purple in late spring, followed by a second flush of single blooms in early autumn. Its restrained size compared to older Jackmanii-type climbers makes it a strong choice for patio containers, pillars, or small trellises where a full-sized vine would be unwieldy. Prune lightly in late winter as a Group 2 clematis, removing only dead or weak growth so the plant keeps the stems that carry the heaviest spring flowering.

common_name: Beth Currie Clematis (Violet Large-Flowered Clematis with Crimson Bar)

planting.note: Plant with the crown shaded and a couple of inches below soil level, training the vine onto a trellis, wall support, or large container obelisk in full sun to partial shade.

directions: Raised in England by Frank Meechan and introduced through Raymond Evison's Guernsey nursery, Beth Currie bears overlapping plum-purple petals marked with a crimson central bar and reddish-cream anthers, opening from May into June with a lighter repeat flowering on new growth later in summer. Its moderate growth rate and compact habit suit it to growing through roses, conifers, or other wall-trained shrubs as well as large patio pots. Give it at least six hours of direct sun for the best flower color, with afternoon shade in hot climates to prevent fading, and prune lightly as a Group 2 clematis.

common_name: Giselle Clematis (Dusky Purple-Pink Compact Patio Clematis)

planting.note: Plant in a large container or small bed with the roots shaded, training stems up a compact obelisk, trellis, or patio support; also useful trailing over a pot edge as groundcover.

directions: Launched by Raymond Evison as part of the compact Boulevard patio collection, Giselle carries dusky purple-pink, star-shaped flowers with pointed sepals accented by deeper purple stamens, blooming almost continuously from late spring until early autumn. Its small stature and free-flowering habit make it one of the easiest clematis for pots, patios, and tight spaces, including training it along the ground as a flowering groundcover. Prune hard in late winter or early spring, cutting all stems back to about 6 inches, since it flowers on new growth as a Group 3 clematis.

common_name: Kenora Sunset Dahlia (Yellow and Flame-Orange Semi-Cactus Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once soil has warmed after the last frost, staking tall stems at planting time to avoid root damage later.

directions: A member of the Kenora series of Canadian-bred exhibition dahlias named for Kenora, Ontario, Kenora Sunset produces medium-sized semi-cactus blooms in a warm blend of yellow and flame-orange with narrow, slightly twisted ray florets. The tall, sturdy stems make it a good cut flower as well as a show bench entry, but benefit from staking and regular disbudding of side buds for the largest blooms. Lift and store tubers over winter in zones colder than 8, dividing clumps in spring before replanting.

common_name: AC Rooster Dahlia (Red Stellar Dahlia with Back-Curving Petals)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once soil has warmed after the last frost.

directions: Introduced by hybridizer Ken Greenway, AC Rooster is a stellar-form dahlia whose fine, feathery red petals sweep back and recurve toward the stem, occasionally streaked with yellow at the base to create a distinctive pinwheel silhouette reminiscent of a rooster's tail. The brighter red upper surface contrasts with a paler underside, giving the bloom extra depth under garden light. Disbud side shoots for larger exhibition-quality flowers, or leave the plant to branch freely for more numerous cutting-garden blooms, and lift tubers for winter storage where the ground freezes.

common_name: Alauna Clair-Obscur Dahlia (Burgundy-to-White Ombre Cactus Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once soil has warmed after the last frost, spacing plants to allow air circulation around the large blooms.

directions: Part of the French-bred Alauna series of fringed cactus dahlias, Clair-Obscur shades dramatically from deep burgundy-purple at the base through violet to pure white fringed tips, giving each 6 to 8 inch bloom a striking ombre effect. The dramatic two-tone color and long, sturdy stems make it a favorite for cutting gardens and mixed bouquets through midsummer into early fall. Stake plants at planting time and disbud selectively to keep bloom size large, then lift and store tubers over winter in zones colder than 8.

common_name: Gallery Renoir Dahlia (Compact Dark Pink Decorative Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 3-4 inches deep in containers or border fronts once soil has warmed after the last frost; no staking needed given its dwarf habit.

directions: Bred by Aad Verwer from a cross of 'Tout a Toi' and 'Oriental Dream', Gallery Renoir is a dwarf decorative dahlia in the painter-named Gallery series, bearing fully double, dark-pink blooms about 4 inches across whose florets fade to pinkish-white toward the edges. Its compact, freely branching habit and rapid, early flowering make it well suited to patio pots, window boxes, and small garden beds rather than cutting rows. No disbudding or staking is required thanks to its naturally dense, upright form, and tubers should be lifted for winter storage in zones colder than 8.

common_name: Pennine Alfie Chrysanthemum (Bronze-Flushed Yellow Spoon-Type Mum)

planting.note: Plant rooted spring cuttings after the last frost into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, pinching young stems once to encourage branching for a fuller autumn display.

directions: Pennine Alfie is a bushy, single-flowered chrysanthemum bearing light yellow blooms flushed with bronze, their spoon-shaped florets giving the flowerheads an airy, distinctive texture in early autumn. It belongs to the popular Pennine series of garden-hardy mums bred for reliable late-season color and good weather resistance. Deadhead spent flowerheads to extend the display, and cut plants back close to the ground after frost, leaving the basal foliage to overwinter and resprout the following spring.

common_name: Golden Woolman's Glory Chrysanthemum (Single-Flowered Golden Garden Mum)

planting.note: Plant rooted spring cuttings after the last frost in full sun and fertile, well-drained soil, pinching once in late spring to build a bushier plant before flower buds set.

directions: A golden-flowered sport of the long-grown single-flowered garden chrysanthemum 'Woolman's Glory', this selection produces tall sprays of golden single blooms with a darker central disc, flowering reliably into the heart of autumn. Its height and classic daisy form make it a traditional choice for cutting gardens and late-season borders alongside asters and ornamental grasses. Support the tall stems with discreet staking or grow-through netting, and divide clumps every two to three years in spring to keep plants vigorous.

common_name: Vagabond Prince Chrysanthemum (Semi-Double Cyclamen-Pink Hardy Mum)

planting.note: Plant rooted spring cuttings or divisions after the last frost in full sun on well-drained soil, pinching the tips once in early summer to promote bushier late-season growth.

directions: Bred by Amos Perry in the early 1950s, Vagabond Prince is a tough, garden-hardy chrysanthemum carrying layered, semi-double cyclamen-pink blooms from late September through November, well after most summer perennials have faded. Its reliable winter hardiness compared with many florist-type mums lets it be left in the ground over winter in favorable climates rather than lifted and stored. Site it in a sunny, well-drained spot sheltered from strong wind, and divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Doctor Tom Parr Chrysanthemum (Semi-Pompon Bronze-Red Garden Mum)

planting.note: Plant rooted spring cuttings after the last frost into fertile, free-draining borders or containers in full sun, pinching once in late spring to build a compact, well-branched plant.

directions: Doctor Tom Parr is a late-season garden chrysanthemum prized for its deep bronze-red, semi-pompon blooms that carry a warm, burnished glow in low autumn light, forming tidy rounded heads above compact, mid-green foliage. It is a weather-tolerant cultivar that continues flowering well into late autumn even after cooler, wetter spells that can spoil more delicate mums. Grow it in a sunny, free-draining spot or large container, and cut plants back near the ground after the display fades, mulching the crown in cold climates.
